current.text: He plays for Detroit and is the projected starting power forward in place of Tobias Harris.
Detroit's power forward depth behind him is weak.
He should play about 30 to 31 minutes, as Tobias Harris did. Detroit may also give him more stability and some extra usage.
If Ron Holland develops a shot, Holland could cut into his minutes.
One expert says coach J.B. Bickerstaff cannot be trusted on what he says about minutes, so planned minutes may not hold.
He becomes a category-league value if he plays 31 minutes.
In category leagues he is a fine pick in rounds 9 to 10. A Yahoo rank around 116 is fair and an ESPN rank around 99 is a bit high.
Experts agree he has little upside. One still calls him underrated at an ADP around 118 because of his solid points, rebounds and percentages.
He should finish above about 120th in rank, but he will not return to his prime level and is no longer a 20 and 10 player.
His rebounds and free throws are expected to recover. He is usually about an eight-rebound player.
Experts see him as a real-life downgrade from Tobias Harris and a worse fit for Detroit.
Detroit plays 4-3-4 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21. The team has 15 back-to-backs, and no rest risks are expected.
Detroit is projected to win 50 to 51 games and finish as a third or fourth seed in the East.

durable.text: He is an off-ball finisher who spaces the corners and cuts. He does not create his own shot.
He shoots a good percentage from three on few attempts, and his three-point shooting is streaky.
He is a passive big with a high FG% and good free throws. He rarely passes, and assists are his weakest category.
He lifts FG% on moderate volume. His FG% is his best category against the top 250 pool.
He is a weak defender, and his defensive stats have dropped.
Experts disagree on his rebounding. One calls him a modest rebounder. Another says he has been a good offensive rebounder throughout his career and is usually about an eight-rebound player.
He is worth more in category leagues than in points leagues.

note: Both sites rank him around 96 to 97 but value him at only 3 to 4 USD, and our league paid 7 USD last season. That makes him a low-cost, low-upside starter at about 1 to 5 USD. He fits any build as a high FG% big with decent FT% and some threes, but he adds almost nothing in assists. Early in the season, check that he reaches 30 to 31 minutes, that his rebounds move back toward 7 to 8, and whether Ron Holland's role grows.
